questions.subject: PHYSICS_EM
questions.topic: The cutoff condition and the single-mode band
questions.learningObjective: Compute the cutoff frequency of a rectangular waveguide
questions.stem: An amateur astronomer's log notes a rectangular waveguide 2.286 cm wide; what is its dominant-mode cutoff frequency in GHz?
questions.explanation: Cutoff frequency equals c over twice the wide dimension. Using c = 3e8 m/s gives 6.56 GHz. A common slip is to double the width again.
questions.hint: Use f_c = c/(2a) with a in metres.

questions.subject: PHYSICS_EM
questions.topic: Guide wavelength above the cutoff
questions.learningObjective: Compute guide wavelength from free-space wavelength and cutoff
questions.stem: Mira records free-space wavelength 3 cm and cutoff wavelength 4 cm; what is the guide wavelength in cm?

options.text: A guide wavelength of 3.6 cm comes from the standard guide-wavelength relation.
A guide wavelength of 1.5 cm comes from halving the free-space value.
options.misconception: halves free-space wavelength instead of combining terms

options.text: A guide wavelength of 5.0 cm comes from adding the two wavelengths.
options.misconception: adds wavelengths instead of using the reciprocal relation

options.text: A guide wavelength of 4.0 cm sets guide wavelength equal to cutoff wavelength.
options.misconception: confuses cutoff wavelength with guide wavelength

questions.explanation: Guide wavelength is lambda_g = lambda_0 / sqrt(1 - (lambda_0/lambda_c)^2). With 3 and 4 cm that gives 3.6 cm. Adding or halving are not valid.

questions.topic: Phase and group velocity in a guide
questions.learningObjective: Compute group velocity from phase velocity and cutoff
questions.stem: A log entry gives phase velocity 4e8 m/s and cutoff wavelength 6 cm with free-space wavelength 4 cm; what is group velocity in m/s?
